name: John McDonald

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, McDonald lists his occupation as TriMet hydro technician.
McDonald's pamphlet statement lists his occupational background as journalist.
McDonald's pamphlet statement lists a BS in political science from Troy University.
McDonald's city filing form lists service as a Broward County, Florida Democratic Party precinct committeeman in 2016.
bio.excerpt: Broward County, Florida Democratic Party Precinct Committeeman, 2016.

source.publisher: City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, McDonald says he wants to keep the Trail Blazers in Portland and modernize the Moda Center.
positions.excerpt: Keep the Trail Blazers in Portland — and modernize the Moda Center.

positions.statement: McDonald's pamphlet statement calls for keeping the Interstate Bridge Replacement Project on track.
positions.excerpt: Ensure the Interstate Bridge Replacement Project stays on track.

positions.statement: McDonald's pamphlet statement calls for repairing streets and cleaning up the transit system.
positions.excerpt: Repair our streets and clean up our transit system.

positions.statement: McDonald's pamphlet statement says he would examine department budgets, inspect facilities and root out waste, fraud and abuse.
positions.excerpt: Examine department budgets, inspect facilities and root out waste, fraud and abuse.

positions.statement: McDonald's pamphlet statement calls for limiting new contracts and demanding accountability from current providers.
positions.excerpt: Limit new contracts and demand accountability from current providers.

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, McDonald says Portland should recruit companies that will bring good jobs.
positions.excerpt: we should recruit companies that will bring good jobs to Portland

positions.statement: In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, McDonald says he would bring a balanced approach to governing and avoid ideological games.
positions.excerpt: bring a balanced, level-headed approach to governing and avoid getting bogged down in ideological games.

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 12 District 4 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form (linked from portland.gov 2026 city candidates page); (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the two articles that profile every District 4 candidate: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 4 council race' (2026-10-07) and Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 4' (2026-09-11). Multi-winner race: OPB states three District 4 seats are on the ballot. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Filing form gives occupation 'Service worker'; pamphlet gives 'TriMet Hydro Technician' (recorded).
